H.answer:
According to the holding in Adair v. United States (1908) (ID: 208_0161-01), it is not within the power of Congress to make it a criminal offense against the United States for a carrier engaged in interstate commerce to discharge an employee simply because of their membership in a labor organization. The provision to that effect in § 10 of the act of June 1, 1898, concerning interstate carriers, is an invasion of personal liberty and the right of property guaranteed by the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution of the United States, and is therefore unenforceable.

Therefore, under the binding doctrine of Adair v. United States (1908), it would not be constitutional to enforce federal legislation prohibiting yellow-dog employment contracts on interstate railroads, as this would violate the Fifth Amendment liberty of contract. (ID: 208_0161-01)
